ic_name: LIN bus 2.2A (Local Interconnect Network, LIN Consortium)
protocol_type: Single-master schedule-table-driven serial bus on a single wire (LIN bus line). Each frame = header from master + response from one publishing slave. Byte-oriented (UART framing on each non-break byte).

break_field.note: Break is the only field that does not comply with the UART byte-field structure. A break/sync sequence shall always be detectable by slave tasks; an in-progress frame shall be aborted and processing of the new frame shall commence on a break/sync detection.

frame_structure.sync_byte_purpose: Slaves without a precise time base measure the alternating edges of 0x55 to compute the master's nominal bit time and resynchronise their UART.

protected_identifier.id_bits: ID0..ID5 = bits 0..5 of PID byte (LSB first).

id_categories.name: Signal-carrying frames
id_categories.checksum: classic for LIN 1.x slaves, enhanced for LIN 2.x slaves

id_categories.name: Reserved (LIN extended format)
id_categories.checksum: shall not be used in a LIN 2.x cluster

frame_types.name: Unconditional frame
frame_types.description: IDs 0..59. Always transmitted when its slot is processed. Single publisher, one-or-many subscribers.

frame_types.name: Event-triggered frame
frame_types.description: Designed to increase responsiveness without high polling overhead. Multiple slaves may publish associated unconditional frames; the first data byte of each associated unconditional frame must equal its PID. Collisions are allowed and resolved by switching to a collision-resolving schedule table.

frame_types.name: Sporadic frame
frame_types.description: Group of unconditional frames sharing one slot. Master publishes only if a signal in one of the associated frames has been updated; otherwise the slot is silent.

frame_types.name: Diagnostic frame
frame_types.description: IDs 0x3C (master request) and 0x3D (slave response). Always 8 data bytes. Carry transport-layer PDUs for node configuration / identification / diagnostics. Always classic checksum.

frame_types.name: Reserved frame
frame_types.description: IDs 0x3E and 0x3F. Shall not be used in LIN 2.x clusters.

checksum_models.name: classic
checksum_models.applies_to: Diagnostic frames (0x3C, 0x3D) and frames going to LIN 1.x slaves.

checksum_algorithm: Eight-bit sum with carry, then bit-inverted: sum all bytes; whenever sum ≥ 256 subtract 255 (equivalent to add-with-carry); finally invert the 8-bit result. Receiver adds the received checksum to its intermediate sum; result shall be 0xFF.

schedule_table.frame_slot_definition: T_Frame_Slot = T_base × n (n integer, normally different per slot). Slot must satisfy T_Frame_Slot > jitter + T_Frame_Maximum.
schedule_table.switch_behaviour: Active schedule processed cyclically. Switch request to new schedule is honoured only at the start of the next frame slot — never mid-frame.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: There is no per-byte VALID/READY handshake on the LIN wire.
Master fully owns timing: it issues each header at the time-base tick scheduled in the active schedule table.
A slave's response is implicitly authorised by receipt of a header whose PID it publishes; subscribers simply receive and validate the checksum.
host_interface_assumption: On a node, the LIN protocol is implemented on top of a UART/SCI peripheral or equivalent state machine. There is no LIN-defined CPU host-bus register interface — that is vendor-specific (e.g. LIN transceiver IC + microcontroller UART).
